segments: Page 373 of the Chronography. of the Franks {OCR?}:
and cut off his head.
And when the Franks saw [this], they became even more distressed,
because they supposed that the one who fell was one of the sons of Saladin.
Now the Count,
because his heart was full of deceit,
feared lest victory should be accomplished for the Franks,
and he should be put to shame, he who had advised them not to engage in battle.
He showed the Franks,
as though he, with his faction, were charging against the Arabs to fight.
And when he charged,
the Arabs opened a way for him through their ranks,
because he had an understanding with them,
and they knew that his side was not true to his coreligionists.
And when he passed through,
he left and went toward Tripoli, his city.
And his departure became a great cause of the Franks' defeat,
and no one trusted his fellow any longer.
Nevertheless, because there was no other recourse except engagement,
they joined battle with the Arabs,
and swords were drawn,
yet they were not able to accomplish anything,
because they had been left as those without hope after the departure of the Count.
And the Arabs prevailed over them,
and they captured Guy, the lord of Tiberias,
and Prince Reynald, the lord of Kerak,
and the majority of the Templar brothers and Hospitallers, and others.
And only a few were able to flee.
And when the battle subsided,
Saladin sat inside his tent,
and his nobles gathered to him.
And he commanded, and they brought before him Guy, the husband of the Queen,
the lord of Tiberias,
and Prince Reynald.
And Saladin honored Guy,
and seated him at his side,
and he seated Reynald as well.
Now Guy, because he was burning with thirst,
as soon as he sat down, asked for water.
And Saladin commanded,
and they gave him iced water to drink.
And when he had drunk half,
he gave the other half to Reynald, and he drank.
Saladin, however, said,
"It was not right for you to give him drink without my command."
Then Guy said to the Sultan,
"Imprisonment is itself death;
do not now kill him two deaths."
